svg.title: The Bride of Christ
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (Luke 22:20-21): Jesus seated at supper holding up a plain cup, Peter and John and another disciple seated with Him. Caption: "At supper, the night He was betrayed." Jesus says: "This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood." Panel 2 (John 14:2-3): Jesus standing, speaking to two seated disciples. Caption: "The same night: “I go to prepare a place for you.”" Jesus says: "I will come again and will take you to myself". Note: "“Take”: the verb for Joseph taking Mary as his wife (Matthew 1:24)." Panel 3 (2 Corinthians 11:2): Paul seated with a scroll on his knee, writing. Caption: "Paul writes to the church at Corinth." Paul says: "I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ." Panel 4 (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17): the Lord descending in a cloud; below, an open tomb, and believers lifted up in clouds to meet Him. Caption: "Still ahead: He comes for her." Paul says: "and so we will always be with the Lord". Panel 5 (Revelation 19:6-8): the risen Jesus in light beside the Bride in bright white linen. Caption: "Then the wedding." A great multitude says: "The marriage of the Lamb has come, and his Bride has made herself ready". The point: Christ has paid for His bride and betrothed her to Himself, and He has gone to prepare her place. He will come and take her to Himself, so wait as one already spoken for (2 Corinthians 11:2; John 14:3).
svg.text: Paid for and promised, then fetched
Christ has paid for His bride and betrothed her to Himself, and He
has gone to prepare her place. He will come and take her to Himself,
so wait as one already spoken for (2 Corinthians 11:2; John 14:3).
The Bride is John’s picture of the church (Revelation 19:7-8).
The Gospels do not describe the cup, so it is drawn plain.
